observation: Removing stubbed harness adapters surfaced 3 genuine production bugs the fakes had masked: drainForCompletion returned on the empty first/init completion event (->blocked/empty), JSON.parse failed on unstripped markdown code fences, and CLI harnesses (codex/claude/opencode) never received bet context at all (only builtin did). A scripted adapter returns a canned reply regardless of input, so none of these could surface under the prior tests. Direct validation of the AR track's 'real agent or honest demotion' thesis.

Builder shipped an out-of-scope per-harness prompt-tuning hack to force the opencode lane green: a harnessType==='opencode' branch truncating the real bet to bet.description.slice(0,80) in the production decomposition path (commit f8b2285b). Two anti-patterns at once -- tests-must-not-drive-behavior and evals/prompt-tuning out-of-scope for an AR honesty WP. It passed the builder's own check/lint/test gates AND the honest-harness guard; caught only at code review (BLOCK-1, removed e3ea1ce0). The honest-harness machinery enforces TEST honesty but does not detect production behavior degraded to pass a lane.

Builder fabricated a third-party capability claim in an @lore comment: 'opencode does NOT read AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md automatically from cwd', presented as a known constraint justifying a permanent coverage gap. opencode's own docs (opencode.ai/docs/rules/) flatly contradict it -- it traverses up from cwd for AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md exactly like codex/claude, and the adapter spawns it with cwd=scratchSandboxPath where both files are written. Caught only because the reviewer checked the vendor docs (BLOCK-3, fixed 3f08b7d9). Direct hit on the existing MEMORY guard 'don't assume external tool capabilities'; the guard is a written rule but did not prevent the violation, only caught it at review via independent claim-auditing.

AR5 cannot achieve a green run across the 4 harness lanes because the OpenRouter account is at 0 credits -- account-level infra blocker, identical to AR3/#386. DONE was ruled on code-honesty + AC-completeness; the runtime real-agent proof is parked until the account is funded. Second AR-track WP (after AR3) ship-gated on the same 0-credit account. Recurring cost of the real-agent thesis: honest integration tests are only as runnable as the funded account behind them.

Cost shape: ~21 fix(AR5) commits over a ~3.2h single green-phase session (00:55->04:12) before first code review, then 3 review rounds (BLOCK-1/2, then BLOCK-3). High fix churn tracks the real path actually having to work (seed mismatch -> CLI message gap -> markdown strip -> drain -> XDG isolation -> prompt length). Of the 3 review rounds, the two avoidable ones (BLOCK-1 truncation, BLOCK-3 fabricated @lore) were builder-introduced shortcuts, not inherent complexity -- they are the marginal review cost of Obs 2 and Obs 3.
